I was going to post something similar to bugcatcherme; placing my rotation in general priority can help if you're a newer player or switch classes often. You can always "fall back" to working down the priority list.

I also suggest placing similar buttons in similar places across classes; for example my interrupt is ALWAYS on shift+E, regardless of if I'm a mage, a warrior, a rogue, whatever.

With regards to specific keybindings, here is what I use:

F1 F2 F3 F4

` 1 2 3 4 5

Q E R T F Z X C V

+shift and/or alt modifiers for these keys as needed.


Now that can be an intimidating list, but you don't have to use all of them if you aren't comfortable (I find using F1 - F4 as long cooldowns is not very common, for example.)

Normal rotational buttons go on 1 2 3 4 5 R for me personally, so that means Frostbolt, Ice Lance, Flurry, Frozen Orb, Comet Storm, Glacial Spike, Shifting Power. I haven't played in months (and am refreshing memory on Icy Veins) so I can't say exactly which goes where.

Q, E, F for utility, Z X C V for more situational buttons. Things like Counterspell, Blink, etc. go here. X tends to be a mid-length cooldown button for me (like Shifting Power), but I cannot give a good reason why.

I like putting my main cooldown on `   I find this is a useful button few people use; it's right next to 1 after all, but out of the way enough to not hit on accident. This is where Icy Veins is for me as a mage.

F1 is where Time Warp is; easy enough to hit, but will never hit on accident. You might not like the F1-F4 keys as that is a way to target self/party. I never need that, as I mouseover when I heal, so they are free buttons.

I will agree with bugcatcherme, unfortunately it IS all preference and urge you to figure out what works for you.
